findings: MINOR - cylinder_pressure_admission._blocking_severity now has a false-positive edge that terminally refuses ordinary nonblocking review prose. Evidence: after the blocking patterns miss, the unknown-label fallback applies `prefix + r'([A-Za-z][A-Za-z_-]*)\s*[:|\-]'` anchored at start (prefix = `^\s*(?:[-*]\s*)?(?:F\d+\s*[:.)-]?\s*)?`) and refuses anything outside allowed={'MINOR','INFO','INFORMATIONAL','NOTE','NONBLOCKING'}. A genuinely MINOR finding beginning 'Remedy: ...', 'Evidence - ...', 'Observation: ...' or 'Recommendation - ...' yields label 'Remedy'/'Evidence'/'Observation'/'Recommendation' -> ValueError('blocking finding contradicts nonblocking verdict'). Because the config and review-receipt SHA256 pins are immutable external inputs, recovery requires a whole new review session and re-pinned config on a max_attempts=1 path. The symmetric false-negative also remains: a mid-sentence severity such as '_prefix burns the ordinal; MAJOR.' matches none of the three blocking patterns (not at start, not bracketed, not followed by ':') and no label pattern ('_' is not in the `[:|\-]` class), so it is admitted under a MINOR verdict. Current tests (test_negated_or_historical_prose_is_not_a_blocking_label, test_explicit_and_unknown_severity_labels_refuse) only assert a fixed sample on both sides, so neither edge is pinned. Remedy: replace the open-ended unknown-label fallback with an explicit severity vocabulary (or require the token to occupy a severity-bearing position: bracketed, after `F\d+`, or after `severity`), and add regressions asserting that 'Remedy:'/'Evidence -' leading prose is admitted and that a trailing/mid-text MAJOR is refused.

MINOR - the authoritative one-shot terminal record has an inconsistent shape: terminal_reasons is present on some paths and absent on others. Evidence: cylinder_pressure_resume._empty() sets only terminal_reason='PRECLAIM_REFUSAL'; the `except Exception` handler sets only terminal_reason='POSTCLAIM_INCOMPLETE'/'PRECLAIM_REFUSAL' plus `error`. terminal_reasons is created solely by _retain (success path) or by _additional_reason, and _additional_reason is only reached when _final_accounting observes a storage FAIL, a negative remaining window, or an accounting exception. So a preclaim refusal (e.g. failure='storage', failure='before_launch') or a postclaim phase2/spawn failure with healthy final accounting writes <parent-stem>.ordinal-2.terminal.json and outcome.json containing terminal_reason but no terminal_reasons key. Since this record is the durable, non-restartable disposition that a later offline parser correction must read, a consumer keying on terminal_reasons will KeyError on exactly the failure records it most needs. test_postclaim_failure_consumes_without_readmission and test_preclaim_refusal_never_launches_or_creates_successor only assert terminal_reason != 'PLANNED_SCOPE_STOP', so the shape is unpinned. Remedy: initialise terminal_reasons in _empty() and set both fields together in the exception handler, then assert the key's presence in every terminal/outcome record test.

MINOR - the newly introduced per-source committed-blob verification runs unbounded Git subprocesses inside the single 600-second invocation window. Evidence: cylinder_pressure_admission.verify_source_commit calls cylinder_runtime_bundle._git_blob(root, revision, row['path']) once per entry of config['source_files'], and _git_blob (cylinder_runtime_bundle.py:56-65) issues two subprocess.run calls per file ('git cat-file -t <rev>' then 'git show <rev>:<name>') with capture_output=True and no timeout=. required_source_inventory forces that list to cover every src/digitalmodel/ansys/*.py plus __init__.py, _compat.py and the entrypoint (~74 paths, ~148 spawns), and the 'cat-file -t' commit check is re-run redundantly for every file. The whole _validate body (verify_source_commit + shared._review, which re-reads and UTF-8-compares the full content of every bundled file, + validate_lineage, which re-enumerates the 23 original files and re-hashes 21 artifacts across three manifests) executes on every verify_authority() call; cylinder_pressure_resume._observe invokes _verify AFTER journal.start() has written the invocation record, so at least one full revalidation is charged to the window before the >=365s preclaim threshold is tested. A hung or slow git (network-backed worktree, filesystem stall) has no bound and cannot be interrupted; the invocation record already exists, so PressureJournal.__init__'s glob(stem + '*') refuses every readmission. Remedy: pass an explicit timeout= to both subprocess.run calls in _git_blob, hoist the 'cat-file -t' commit-type check out of the per-file loop, and add a driver-level test asserting the bounded-timeout contract.

MINOR - cylinder_pressure_capture._check misclassifies missing-evidence failures as dependency/contract defects. Evidence: _independent_checks passes artifacts.get(name) straight into the parsers ('configuration' -> parse_configuration(native), 'model' -> parse_model_cdb, 'state' -> parse_state_values, 'precision_witness' -> validate_precision_witness). When a file is missing, redirected, hardlinked or read-errored, _inventory_row returns raw=None and the name is absent from artifacts, so the parser receives None and typically raises TypeError; _check then records error_class='dependency_or_contract_error' rather than 'evidence_error'. The module already handles this correctly for the two checks that were explicitly guarded ('execution' via `all(isinstance(artifacts.get(name+'.bin'), bytes) ...)` and 'case_titles' via `isinstance(native, bytes)`), so the inconsistency is local. test_dependency_errors_remain_explicit_nonacceptance injects a deliberate broken classify_diagnostics, and test_partial_inventory_continues_after_failure only asserts inventory row status, so the mislabel is uncovered. Impact is diagnostic, not acceptance: capture_status stays INCOMPLETE and accepted_values stays {}, but the immutable capture record that must drive the later reviewed parser correction will attribute an evidence gap to a code defect. Remedy: guard each parsed check with an isinstance(..., bytes) precondition emitting status='INCOMPLETE' with an explicit evidence reason, matching the existing execution/case_titles pattern.
